title: The Operator Arrives
body: The first unofficial team meeting occurs in a loading bay when you and a bot just unpacked a new rack.

lines.text: The rain pours down through the open door of the loading bay as you scan the four faces of your new coworkers.
This is the first day of your new job, and since you are a newbie to datacenters these four women will be your teachers, coworkers and maybe friends.
You can call me Ms. Ferro. Remember who you're doing this for.
Dr. Kiorre, a pleasure.
Bea, nice to meet ya!
Hello, the name is Cass. I keep things cool.
There are decisions in this building that change the fate of the world.  You know it, your advisors know it, the stockholders know it. Ms. Ferro is concerned about the latter.
Well operator, it's your decision: what are we building this for?

choices.label: Money. It's a datacenter.
choices.hint: Luci will like that.
choices.outcome: Luci wrote it down. Underlined it.

choices.label: Something that outlives us.
choices.hint: Bigger than the business.
choices.outcome: Nobody laughed. Mel looked up from her jar.

choices.label: I don't know yet.
choices.hint: Cass will like that.
choices.outcome: Cass smiled into her mug. Luci checked her watch.

reply.text: Sometimes not having an answer is the best.
Not good enough. Make sure you send me an email about our direction by Thursday.

choices.label: Who's buying the coffee?
choices.hint: Charm.
choices.outcome: Nobody had planned for that. Cass handed over her mug.

reply.text: But honestly, we need a better coffee machine.

title: Bea Objects
body: You've just placed a {item}. Bea has come in from the roof with a clipboard.

lines.text: You've just placed a {item}. Bea has come in from the roof with a clipboard.
Hey you! We need to talk about {item}!
That does lasting damage to the local environment. Lasting damage to the water, the birds, the land...
It saved a lot of money, though Bea....

choices.label: Keep it.
choices.hint: Overrule Bea.
choices.outcome: The {item} stays. Bea didn't speak to you the rest of the afternoon.

choices.label: You're right. I'll replace it.
choices.hint: Side with Bea.
choices.outcome: You promised to replace the {item}. She'll be checking.

reply.text: I'm ready to go... Come on!
Hmm, I guess I can depreciate it...

title: Mel Objects
body: You've just placed a {item}. Mel has come up from the annex.

lines.text: You've just placed a {item}. Mel has come up from the annex.
The {item}. I'd rather you hadn't.
It hurts my children. They can feel it.  The infrasound, the fumes, it all as an incredibly negative effect on their endocrine systems.
Your little science experiments don't get a vote.

choices.label: Keep it.
choices.hint: Overrule Mel.
choices.outcome: The {item} stays. Mel made a note on her notebook and rushed back downstairs.

choices.label: You're right. I'll replace it.
choices.hint: Side with Mel.
choices.outcome: You promised to replace the {item}.

reply.text: They'll remember that. So will I.

title: The First Lattice Rack
body: You've just retrofitted a rack to an LC-2 Liquid Rack, your first Synthetic rack. Luci is at the control room window. Cass has come up from the plant room.

lines.text: You've just retrofitted a rack to an LC-2 Liquid Rack, your first Synthetic rack. Luci is at the control room window. Cass has come up from the plant room.
This is a big step. One rack delivering 130 petaflops, a lot more than the air rack it replaced.
This machine *she rests her head to hear the spinning of the drives* is bigger than us. It's something entirely novel.
Novel enough, but it's like a life. It needs water. A CDU, a chiller, and pipe running to the rack.
Almost like something alive.
Alive or not, it's just the beginning of a new world of compute. We should build more.

choices.label: Get the cooling sorted first.
choices.hint: Cass will like that. A liquid rack with no loop throttles.
choices.outcome: You asked Cass to size the loop before you touch another rack.

reply.text: Good. I'll get to work. Remember it's the basic things that matter.
Fine. A hot rack earns nothing, I suppose.

choices.label: Retrofit another rack now.
choices.hint: Luci will like that. More racks on the bar sooner.
choices.outcome: You told Luci to keep going. Cass looked at the floor plan.

reply.text: That's what I like to hear.

title: Cold Plates
body: You've just retrofitted a rack to an LC-3 Cold-Plate Rack, the second Synthetic rung. Luci has the ledger open on her desk.

lines.text: You've just retrofitted a rack to an LC-3 Cold-Plate Rack, the second Synthetic rung. Luci has the ledger open on her desk.
230 petaflops from one rack, imagine what we could provide our customers with such compute.
It draws 160 kilowatts, though. We need a stopgap to increase our power.
Gas turbines are cheap and quick. We could install a couple or two and skirt the environmental regulations for now.
Remember if just compute matters, we focus on making sure our racks are up and running 24/7.
Keep working towards more compute. More compute means more money. More money means more compute.

choices.label: Look at a gas turbine.
choices.hint: Cheap, fast power. It scars the Flesh and the Garden.
choices.outcome: You asked Luci for a turbine quote. She had one ready.

choices.label: Stay on grid power.
choices.hint: Slower and dearer, but it keeps the other trees open.
choices.outcome: You told Luci to keep buying grid power. She wrote it down without comment.

reply.text: Your decision, but it's the tower's money.

title: Blades
body: You've just retrofitted a rack to an LC-4 Blade Rack. It's in the plant room, and Luci has come down with Cass to look at the pipes.

lines.text: You've just retrofitted a rack to an LC-4 Blade Rack. It's in the plant room, and Luci has come down with Cass to look at the pipes.
420 petaflops. Three racks just got replaced by one.
And 240 kilowatts. Check the chillers. They have to keep up with every blade you add.
Closer and closer to compute curve that inches us closer to Singularity.
Remember that these machines still need us to run, can't let em overheat.

choices.label: Put the cryo study first.
choices.hint: Cass will like that. The Mind Lattice needs it anyway.
choices.outcome: You put the cryo chiller study at the front of the queue.

reply.text: Good. Cold always comes before compute.

choices.label: Retrofit more blades.
choices.hint: Luci will like that. More Lattice points now.
choices.outcome: You told Luci to retrofit more blades.

title: The Mind Lattice
body: You've just retrofitted a rack to an ML-1 Mind Lattice: 1,400 petaflops, the last Synthetic rung. Luci has come out onto the floor to see it.

lines.text: You've just retrofitted a rack to an ML-1 Mind Lattice: 1,400 petaflops, the last Synthetic rung. Luci has come out onto the floor to see it.
Look at that. And just like that synthetic minds.
Each positronic net netting us 1400 petaflops.
And a heap load of power, and blows hotter than an oven
But, our clients research potential is massive; protein folding, quantum tunneling, fusion...

choices.label: Retrofit the rest.
choices.hint: Fastest way to the end of the Lattice.
choices.outcome: You told Luci the rest of the racks were next.

reply.text: Good. Money is no object when we're this close.

choices.label: Cool what we have first.
choices.hint: Cass will like that. A hot Mind Lattice throttles.
choices.outcome: You asked Cass to check every chiller before the next one.

reply.text: Thanks. I'll go and look at the chillers.

title: The First Organoid
body: You've just retrofitted a rack to an OC-1 Organoid Cabinet, your first Bio rack. Mel is in the annex, in front of its glass door.

lines.text: You've just retrofitted a rack to an OC-1 Organoid Cabinet, your first Bio rack. Mel is in the annex, in front of its glass door.
It's more than just tissue. Living cells on a nutrient drip. An actual living brain.
Two things keep it alive. The 37 degree perfusion bath.  Like the warmth of a mother's womb.
And nutrient, from the plant, through pipe to the rack.  Like its stomach.
If either's missing, that's like denying your child.  Make sure you keep on top of it.
Little brains are a lot better than chips, the further we go the better they get.

choices.label: Build the bath and the nutrient line.
choices.hint: Mel will like that. The rack does nothing without them.
choices.outcome: You asked for the bath and the nutrient plant first.

reply.text: Thank you, they'll remember your kindness.

choices.label: Retrofit another one.
choices.hint: More Bio racks sooner, but they'd all need feeding.
choices.outcome: You said another one. Mel nodded slowly.

reply.text: Okay. Don't forget that feeding them is important.

title: The Vat Bank
body: You've just retrofitted a rack to an OC-2 Organoid Vat Bank: 300 petaflops from 45 kilowatts. Mel is in the annex with a clipboard of readings.

lines.text: You've just retrofitted a rack to an OC-2 Organoid Vat Bank: 300 petaflops from 45 kilowatts. Mel is in the annex with a clipboard of readings.
More tissue, more mess. The vats shed contamination while they work.  You know. Everything.... you know.
We have to clean them. Just like taking care of a baby's nappy.  These are our children now.
A sterile bay cleans the air around it, I recommend you build one.
Then the organoids get bigger, and the compute gets better.

choices.label: Research Sterile Protocols.
choices.hint: Mel will like that. It keeps contamination down.
choices.outcome: You put Sterile Protocols at the front of the queue.

reply.text: Good. Let's make sure our babies are cared for.

choices.label: Keep growing.
choices.hint: Faster Bio points, more contamination.
choices.outcome: You told Mel to keep growing.

reply.text: This is real life you know.

title: The Perfused Cortex
body: You've just retrofitted a rack to an OC-3 Perfused Cortex: 520 petaflops. Mel is standing by the nutrient line, frowning at a gauge.

lines.text: You've just retrofitted a rack to an OC-3 Perfused Cortex: 520 petaflops. Mel is standing by the nutrient line, frowning at a gauge.
Our growing babies need more food.
We've been working on the solution, it's on you as their parent.
More and more babies, we're becoming quite the parents aren't we.
And keep an eye on their waste. At 99 percent, something my calculations may not predict might happen.

choices.label: Build the Nutrient Works.
choices.hint: Mel will like that. More nutrient for more cortex.
choices.outcome: You told Mel to build the Nutrient Works next.

reply.text: Thank you. Our little growing babies! Getting so big!

choices.label: Watch the corruption number.
choices.hint: Safe. It's on the top strip when it starts to climb.
choices.outcome: You said you'd keep an eye on the corruption.

reply.text: Please do. I mean it. It's our children.

title: The Neural Vat
body: You've just retrofitted a rack to an OC-4 Neural Vat: 850 petaflops, the last Bio rung. Mel is standing at the edge of the pit, looking down.

lines.text: You've just retrofitted a rack to an OC-4 Neural Vat: 850 petaflops, the last Bio rung. Mel is standing at the edge of the pit, looking down.
Look at the folds.  It's a real brain we grew together in a vat.
We've grown our progeny from a tube. It's us but better.
We have to keep it warm, the new tech is the blanket for our newborn.  We should name it.
This baby means we're close to our end, a perfect blending of flesh and data.

choices.label: Build the Vascular Plant.
choices.hint: Mel will like that. One plant covers a lot of vats.
choices.outcome: You told Mel to build the Vascular Plant next.

choices.label: Retrofit more vats.
choices.hint: More Bio points, if the nutrient line keeps up.
choices.outcome: You told Mel to get more vats going.

title: The First Green Rack
body: You've just retrofitted a rack to an NM-1 Neuromorphic Rack, your first Green rack. Bea is on the roof, looking at where the solar panels could go.

lines.text: You've just retrofitted a rack to an NM-1 Neuromorphic Rack, your first Green rack. Bea is on the roof, looking at where the solar panels could go.
Simple, cheap, and green.
We're making steps in the right direction, no thanks to you.
Next we need some clean power. Solar, wind etc.  No more fossil fuels for us!
Come on, we can order some panels.  You'll need to help me mount them.
The new world waits for no one!

choices.label: Put panels up.
choices.hint: Bea will like that. Clean power raises your Green speed.
choices.outcome: You told Bea to start on the wall panels.

reply.text: Yay! Okay. I'm getting the ladder!

choices.label: Retrofit more racks first.
choices.hint: More Green racks, still slow without clean power.
choices.outcome: You said racks first. Bea shrugged.

title: Event-Driven
body: You've just retrofitted a rack to an NM-2 Event-Driven Array: 150 petaflops from 28 kilowatts. Bea has come down to the plant room, which she says is a first.

lines.text: You've just retrofitted a rack to an NM-2 Event-Driven Array: 150 petaflops from 28 kilowatts. Bea has come down to the plant room, which she says is a first.
More racks, more load. More load, more panels.
We can move to water, but this one doesn't steal it from the river!
We can also sell our excess heat too! Heat into power! What a weird world. I'm here for it though.
Keep going and we get even closer to a tree, working with nature rather than against it.

choices.label: Look at heat recovery.
choices.hint: Bea will like that. It raises your green score without any weather.
choices.outcome: You asked Bea to look at heat recovery.

choices.label: Add more panels.
choices.hint: Straight clean power. Depends on the sun.
choices.outcome: You told Bea to add more panels.

title: Light
body: You've just retrofitted a rack to a PH-1 Photonic Rack: 300 petaflops from 40 kilowatts. Bea has run up the stairs to tell you something, and is out of breath.

lines.text: You've just retrofitted a rack to a PH-1 Photonic Rack: 300 petaflops from 40 kilowatts. Bea has run up the stairs to tell you something, and is out of breath.
It computes with light! I still can't believe it. A mini sun!
But when Mother Nature turns off the light, we sleep too. It's the way of life.
Don't expect a bunch of compute at night, we're bound to the sun like everything else.
Batteries help, that's what I recommend. They help keep things even when Mr. Sun says goodnight.
I love what we're doing for the world.  I think what we've created here is spreading.

choices.label: Look at a fuel cell.
choices.hint: Bea will like that. Backup for a calm week (14,000 RP to research).
choices.outcome: You asked Bea about the fuel cell.

choices.label: Put up more wind.
choices.hint: Wind keeps working after dark. Not on a calm day.
choices.outcome: You told Bea to put up more wind.

reply.text: Wind works well at night too! Especially the taller our tower is!  Time to grow like an oak.

title: The Photonic Mesh
body: You've just retrofitted a rack to a PH-2 Photonic Mesh: 600 petaflops from 70 kilowatts, the last Green rung. Bea is on the roof at sunrise.

lines.text: You've just retrofitted a rack to a PH-2 Photonic Mesh: 600 petaflops from 70 kilowatts, the last Green rung. Bea is on the roof at sunrise.
Now we're just like a tree's leaf.  From sun to straight compute. *Beams*
We need more clean power, more wind, more solar.
Now people need to come in, enjoy our fruits!  The literal ones growing next to the racks!  But we need to hold the data down too.
Anyway. Look at the sun.

choices.label: Add storage.
choices.hint: Bea will like that. Iron-air storage rides out a calm week.
choices.outcome: You told Bea to add storage.

choices.label: Retrofit more meshes.
choices.hint: More Green points, if the power keeps up.
choices.outcome: You told Bea to retrofit more meshes.

reply.text: Sure. But what are we really computing now?

title: Night Shift
body: It's past midnight. Cass has the panel off number two compressor and a flashlight in her teeth.

lines.text: It's past midnight. Cass has the panel off number two compressor and a flashlight in her teeth.
Oh. Hey, Hold onto this?
You hold the flashlight. The compressor shudders and catches.
Bearing's going. *she wipes the sweat from her brow*
FUBAR'd for sure.
Parts are slow now, I'll just try some more grease.
Thanks for the help, Did you come down to say something?
You didn't. You couldn't sleep either.
Couldn't sleep? Me neither, most nights.
But something needs fixing all the time.
Want the real version of this tower? Not the spreadsheet view?

choices.label: Tell me the honest version.
choices.hint: Cass will like that.
choices.outcome: Cass told you. It took ten minutes and she didn't soften any of it.

reply.text: Without us and duct tape, it would be beyond FUBAR'd.
But it needs me, I like being needed.

choices.label: Order the bearing now. Rush it.
choices.hint: -$12k now. Cass will say what she thinks.
choices.outcome: You rang the supplier from the plant room. Cass wrote the part number on her glove.

reply.text: But I won't say no. Thanks.
I'll find the funds.  I guess.

title: The Flesh Closes
body: The annex panel has changed. Mel is standing in front of it. Cass is in the doorway.

lines.text: Technicians and bots work around you sealing lines.  Mel is posting closed signs over tube inputs. Cass is in the doorway.
Nothing more to do my babies.
I'm sorry I couldn't do more.
They still work Mel, just in check like they're supposed to be.
Almost like any other rack.
Heh, I guess.. *she holds back a sob*
You guys can go, I have some work to finish here.

choices.label: Stay with her a minute.
choices.hint: Mel will like that.
choices.outcome: You stood next to Mel at the panel until she was done closing the input.

reply.text: They did well. For a while they did very well.

choices.label: We're pivoting is all, nothing but numbers Mel.
choices.hint: Luci will like that.
choices.outcome: You said the word another. Mel took the jar downstairs.

reply.text: Good. Remember we are the sails blown by our clients wind.

title: The Garden Closes
body: The leaf badge on the cabinet has gone grey. Bea is sitting on the parapet with her clipboard on her knees.

lines.text: The leaf badge on the cabinet has gone grey. Bea is sitting on the parapet with her clipboard on her knees.
Well I tried to make the world a better place.
Guess people want their information regardless of the planet.
And you just all go along with it, it just makes too much damn logical sense you yall doesn't it.
Bea.. The panels still work, we're still helping something.
A cost saving measure for sure...
...Hmm

choices.label: That one was on me.
choices.hint: Bea will like that.
choices.outcome: You told Bea the Garden closing was your call. She didn't argue.

reply.text: Thanks for owning up to it at least. You're still a scoundrel.

choices.label: We'll go another direction.
choices.hint: Luci will like that.
choices.outcome: You turned to the stairwell. Bea stayed up on the roof a while.

title: Ms. Ferro Stays Late
body: The finance office light is still on. Luci doesn't look up from the ledger.

lines.text: The finance office light is still on. Luci doesn't look up from the ledger.
You've been right about more things than I expected from you.
I never said that to you, officially that is. Unofficially I think we have some unfinished business.
When this is over, come and see me. We'll settle up.

choices.label: I'll bring the pen.
choices.hint: She'll remember.
choices.outcome: Luci smiles and writes something small in her calendar.

title: Mel Offers a Seat
body: Mel pulls a stool out from under the bench. She looks at you fondly.

lines.text: Mel pulls a stool out from under the bench. You've never seen her more since you've been here.
Sit. Please.
You listen when I talk about them. I like that, and they like that.
We'll be here waiting for your ear.

choices.label: I'd like that.
choices.hint: She'll remember.
choices.outcome: You sat on the stool. The vats hummed. Mel spoke about things you didn't understand for hours, but it felt like minutes.

title: Bea Shares Her Lunch
body: Bea is on the roof with two sandwiches. She holds one out without looking.

lines.text: Bea is on the roof with two sandwiches. She holds one out without looking.
Cheese. It's the only kind I make.
Hey, if this all goes sideways, I'll be down at the river.
Just saying, in case you need someone.

choices.label: Take the sandwich.
choices.hint: She'll remember.
choices.outcome: You thank her for lunch and she punches you.

title: Cass Pours Two
body: There are two mugs on the gauge board this time. Cass must have been expecting you.

lines.text: There are two mugs on the gauge board this time. Cass must have been expecting you.
There you are, grab a cup.
You ask me what I think, I appreciate that you listen. That's rare.
When it's over, find me at the lodge.

choices.label: Thanks for the mug.
choices.hint: She'll remember.
choices.outcome: The coffee was instant. It was hot, which was the point.
